chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halbi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meal, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Adhere to vinegar and oil, for it is nourishing. Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to eat it frequently, and I eat it frequently, and it is nourishing.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imams recommend for a healthy and nourishing diet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) recommends vinegar and olive oil as a staple diet, citing their nutritional benefits and noting that both he and Imam Ali (AS) frequently consumed them. This practice reflects the Prophetic tradition of simplicity and health, emphasizing that such a basic diet is sufficient for maintaining strength and well-being. The emphasis on 'eating much' (ikthar al-akl) suggests that these foods are easily digestible and sustaining, aligning with Shia emphasis on following the dietary habits of the Ahl al-Bayt for spiritual and physical purity.
